papers.title: Dental Principles for Plastic Surgery.
papers.abstract: LEARNING OBJECTIVES: After studying this article, the participant should be able to: 1. Understand the relevant dental anatomy, chronicity, nomenclature, and diagnostic imaging. 2. Identify dental pathologies, including congenital abnormalities and dentofacial developmental disorders. 3. Review management strategies for dental infections or trauma. 4. Highlight the role of orthodontics in orthognathic and craniofacial reconstructive surgery. SUMMARY: Craniofacial surgery requires a thorough understanding of dental pathology and basic orthodontic principles to treat patients presenting with complex congenital disorders, trauma, and maxillomandibular discrepancies. Despite the close relationship between dentistry, orthodontics, and plastic surgery that dates to the late 1800s, there is a dearth of formalized education of basic dental and orthodontic concepts within plastic surgery curricula. This article outlines basic principles of dental anatomy, dental anomalies, and technology managed by orthodontists to optimize the multidisciplinary approach to craniomaxillofacial pathology.

papers.title: Linking Empathy to Psychological Intimate Partner Violence: The Mediation Analysis of Two Competitive Mediating Pathways.
papers.abstract: While empathy training has long been considered a cornerstone of clinical interventions for intimate partner violence (IPV), emerging evidence on the link between empathy and IPV perpetration suggests an inconsistent association. Guided by the double-edged sword theory and integrating attachment theoretical perspectives within the Chinese cultural context, this study established a competitive mediation model to explain this counterintuitive relationship. An online sample from 31 provinces in China, including 295 adults (69.8% women; Mage = 29.50 years), completed questionnaires measuring empathy, emotion appraisal, attachment avoidance, attachment anxiety, and psychological IPV perpetration. Results suggested that empathy may be indirectly associated with higher psychological IPV perpetration through attachment anxiety, while simultaneously linked to lower psychological IPV perpetration through a mediation chain of emotion appraisal and attachment avoidance. These two competitive mediating pathways mutually canceled each other, potentially accounting for an apparent lack of association between empathy and psychological IPV perpetration. These findings suggested the necessity of screening for insecure attachment styles before empathy-based IPV intervention. For perpetrators with avoidant attachment, empathy training may be enhanced by incorporating emotion appraisal, whereas for perpetrators with anxious attachment, empathy interventions may warrant caution.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted fluorescence immunochromatographic detection of Salmonella typhimurium in complex food matrices via tannic acid-enhanced AIE nanoprobes.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rapid on-site detection of Salmonella typhimurium in complex food matrices remains challenging due to the need for fluorescent probes that maintain intense emission in aqueous environments while resisting interference from salts and pH fluctuations. In this work, we explore tannic acid (TA) as a non-covalent interfacial modifier to construct SiO2/TCPE/TA (STT) nanoparticles for fluorescence immunochromatographic assays (ICA). Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations reveal that TA interacts with the aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) TCPE through cooperative π-π stacking and hydrogen bonding, which stabilizes the excited state, slightly narrows the energy gap, and suppresses non-radiative decay pathways. RESULTS: Guided by the theoretical predictions, we synthesize STT nanoparticles featuring uniform spherical morphology, tunable size, and a TA-enriched surface. The TA modification boosts the absolute fluorescence quantum yield from 12.91% to 30.51% and extends the fluorescence lifetime from 1.79 ns to 2.57 ns. Taking advantage of these improved photophysical properties, the STT-based ICA strip achieves a visual detection limit of 500 CFU mL-1 and a quantitative limit of 128 CFU mL-1 for S. typhimurium. Practical applicability is confirmed in spiked milk, chicken, and lettuce samples, with recoveries ranging from 82.75% to 119.29%. Moreover, a machine-learning classifier trained on strip images from the three food matrices attains perfect classification accuracy across five concentration levels, enabling automated and objective result reading. SIGNIFICANCE: This work presents a non-covalent confinement strategy to engineer bright and robust AIE nanoprobes. By combining mechanistic insights from DFT calculations with experimental validation, the TA-mediated approach not only enhances fluorescence performance but also ensures matrix tolerance. papers.title: Dodecylamine-promoted persistence of ultrasonication-generated microbubbles and its implications for quartz flotation.
papers.abstract: Dodecylamine (DDA), a cationic surfactant widely used in quartz flotation, can promote microbubble formation during ultrasonication; however, these ultrasonication-generated (UG) microbubbles may rapidly dissolve once the ultrasonic field is removed. This study hypothesizes that combining DDA with air oversaturation can markedly suppress post-ultrasonication microbubble dissolution and thereby enhance quartz flotation. UG bulk and surface microbubbles were characterized using dissolved-air measurements and optical imaging, while surface tension and contact angle measurements were used to elucidate the role of DDA. Flotation performance was evaluated using bubble pick-up and micro-flotation tests. DDA markedly increases the population of persistent UG microbubbles under air-oversaturated conditions, whereas no clear DDA-induced increase is observed under non-oversaturated conditions. This behavior is consistent with the coupled effects of air oversaturation and the DDA-induced reduction in gas-liquid interfacial tension, which together enhance the diffusive stability of microbubbles. The unexpectedly rapid decrease in bubble contact angle following bubble-solid contact in DDA solution suggests possible interfacial redistribution of DDA from the solid surface to the gas-liquid interface, which may accelerate the local reduction in gas-liquid interfacial tension. The resulting larger population of persistent microbubbles markedly enhances quartz-particle attachment to carrier bubbles and improves flotation recovery, highlighting the coupled roles of air oversaturation and surfactant adsorption in ultrasound-assisted flotation.

papers.title: Decoupling pore size and porosity in Voronoi bone scaffolds: A multiphysics framework for early osteogenic evaluation.
papers.journal: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
papers.abstract: The irregular, trabecular-like morphology of Voronoi-tessellated scaffolds makes them attractive for bone tissue engineering. However, most existing Voronoi modelling methods cannot independently control pore size and porosity, restricting systematic evaluation of scaffold structure-function relationships. This study developed a discrete element method (DEM)-based Voronoi modelling framework that decouples pore size from porosity. A coupled multiphysics evaluation strategy was established, integrating static compression, computational fluid dynamics, discrete phase modelling, and mechano-regulation analysis. This framework assessed mechanical behaviour, mass transport, early MSC adhesion, and hematoma-stage osteogenic potential. Porosity primarily governed scaffold stiffness, whereas permeability was more sensitive to pore size. MSC adhesion was closely associated with specific surface area and was jointly regulated by transport accessibility and attachment area. Fluid shear stress contributed more to the composite mechanical stimulus than solid-phase strain across all scaffold designs, indicating that fluid-mediated stimulation dominated the local osteogenic microenvironment. The predicted mechano-regulated osteogenic potential was not maximized by any single structural parameter. Instead, it emerged from a balance between MSC capture efficiency and the adequacy of mechanical stimulation. These findings support a "capture-then-differentiate" mechanism for early osteogenesis in Voronoi scaffolds. The framework provides quantitative guidance for site-specific Voronoi scaffold design and a generalizable strategy for evaluating porous architectures from coupled biomechanical and biological perspectives.

papers.title: Cotton gauze coated with Zr-MOF adsorbent for in-tip solid phase extraction of parabens from personal care products.
papers.abstract: A composite adsorbent was fabricated by dip-coating cotton gauze with a Zr-based metal-organic framework (Zr-MOF) dispersed in a chitosan solution. The cotton gauze provided a supporting material for the Zr-MOF adsorbent. The composite adsorbent was applied to extract four parabens from personal care products by in-tip solid-phase extraction. The Zr-MOF was prepared in a one-step solvothermal process, using Zr ions and an organic ligand. The adsorption of target analytes was enabled by hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interactions, and π-π interactions. The extracted parabens were determined using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with diode-array detection. Under the optimal conditions, the developed method provided linearity from 1.50 to 100 μg L-1 with a limit of detection of 0.50 μg L-1. Recoveries from spiked personal care products were in the range of 71.0 to 103.5 % with acceptable relative standard deviations below 9.0 %. The developed composite adsorbent exhibited high extraction efficiency, good biodegradability, ease of fabrication, and good stability.

papers.title: Interfacial hydrogen bonding and quantum confinement synergistically control triplet-energy-transfer-mediated photocatalysis by perovskite nanocrystals.
papers.abstract: Triplet-energy-transfer (TET) photocatalysis by semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) relies on short-range Dexter transfer across the NC-substrate interface, making catalytic efficiency highly sensitive to both NC photophysics and substrate organization. While lead halide perovskite NCs have recently emerged as potent triplet sensitizers, current strategies largely rely on carboxylate-mediated substrate anchoring to facilitate interfacial TET. Generalizable substrate-organization strategies and their interplay with quantum confinement in governing photocatalytic reactivity remain unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that CsPbBr3 NCs catalyze TET-mediated [2 + 2] photocycloaddition of chalcone derivatives and reveal that interfacial hydrogen bonding and quantum confinement synergistically govern photocatalytic reactivity. Native ammonium ligands of the NCs promote substrate recognition through hydrogen-bonding interactions, organizing chalcone substrates at the NC surface without covalent anchoring. Stern-Volmer analysis and transient absorption spectroscopy reveal pronounced size-dependent TET dynamics, with quantum-confined NCs exhibiting substantially enhanced triplet sensitization. These effects translate directly into photocatalytic performance, enabling efficient intermolecular photocycloadditions of diverse chalcone derivatives and selective heterocoupling with alkene partners through preferential chalcone sensitization. Control experiments further demonstrate that efficient photocatalysis requires both interfacial hydrogen bonding and quantum confinement. This work establishes an interfacial design principle for perovskite-NC triplet photocatalysis and provides new insight into controlling energy-transfer reactions at semiconductor nanocrystal interfaces.

papers.title: Approval Matters Less When the Self Expands: Self-Expansion as a Buffer Against Low Perceived Friend Approval in Same-Gender Interracial Relationships.
papers.abstract: Same-gender interracial couples often encounter unique stressors, including disapproval from friends, which can undermine relationship quality. Drawing on self-expansion theory, we tested whether engaging in novel self-expanding activities with a partner buffers against the negative effects of low perceived friend approval. At Time 1, participants (N = 205) in same-gender interracial relationships were randomly assigned to either a self-expansion condition, in which they completed a novel activity with their partner, or a control condition, in which they were given no additional instructions. As predicted, there was a significant interaction between the self-expansion condition and friend approval at Time 1 on relationship quality at Time 2. Such that, individuals in the self-expansion condition reported higher satisfaction and commitment at Time 2, even when they perceived low levels of friend approval. These effects held when controlling for relationship quality at Time 1. Findings highlight self-expansion as a relational process that promotes resilience against social network stigma, underscoring the importance of novel, growth-oriented activities for supporting relationship well-being in same-gender interracial relationships.

papers.title: Divalent cations enhance nanofiltration of amino acids in multicomponent solution systems: Molecular insights and implication to drinking water treatment.
papers.abstract: Amino acids (AAs), an important precursor to nitrogeneous disinfection byproducts, can pass through nanofiltration (NF) membranes and influence finished water quality. Due to complex natural water compositions, AA rejection by NF involves intricate metal-organic interplays that are difficult to describe using existing macroscopic filtration models. Therefore, this study integrated molecular dynamics simulation with experimental investigation to elucidate NF mechanism of glycine in the multicomponent solution systems. The NF experiment results showed that the presence of divalent cations in the feed solutions increased glycine rejection from a baseline of 42.2% (glycine in pure water) to 52.5% and 58.1% in the presence of Zn2+ and Ca2+, respectively. This trend cannot be explained by steric or dielectric exclusion mechanisms. The MD simulation results reveal that the ternary interactions among glycine, divalent ions and the membrane jointly govern glycine filtration. Specifically, Ca²⁺/ Zn²⁺ competes with glycine for interaction sites on the membrane surface and within the pores, which alters the structure, energetics, and dynamics of respective binary interactions. These changes not only suppresses glycine sorption onto membrane surface, but also elevates the energy barrier for its pore-entry from 29.95 to 36.02-38.74 kcal mol⁻¹, and the barrier for intrapore migration from 16.24 to 26.61-28.93 kcal mol⁻¹. Overall, these findings highlight the existence of coupled interplays among organics, divalent cations and membranes and their relevance to the selectivity of NF membranes for AAs in realistic waters.

papers.title: Sonic-black-hole acoustic focusing for non-contact atomization of silicone oils up to 2000 cP.
papers.abstract: Non-contact ultrasonic atomization of highly viscous liquids is limited by the severe acoustic-impedance mismatch between air and liquid and by viscous suppression of free-surface breakup. Here, we propose a sonic-black-hole non-contact atomizer (SBHNA) incorporating a segmented power-law acoustic focusing cavity to enhance the localization of airborne ultrasonic energy near the atomization outlet. The power-law contraction produces a slow-wave compression region near the nozzle-side turning point and strengthens the interaction between the localized field and the subwavelength outlet-reflection boundary. Theoretical analysis and frequency-domain simulations show that the focal-pressure enhancement is governed by the coupled effects of geometric focusing, slow-wave compression, outlet reflection, and full-cavity phase matching rather than by geometric contraction alone. Atomization experiments demonstrate that the SBHNA incorporating the optimized m = 2.2 power-law focusing cavity enables stable non-contact atomization of 2000 cP silicone oil, producing droplets with a Sauter mean diameter of 51.9 μm and a distribution span of 0.356. This capability highlights the potential of SBH acoustic focusing for aerosol generation, coating, spraying, and processing of highly viscous functional liquids.

papers.title: Parental reflective functioning in attachment-based family therapy for LGBTQ+ young adults and their nonaccepting parents.
papers.abstract: Parental rejection significantly impacts the mental health of sexual and gender minority young adults and can undermine parent-child relationships. Attachment-based family therapy for sexual and gender minorities aims to repair these ruptures by facilitating "corrective episodes," where parents listen to their young adult's experience of feeling rejected and respond with empathy and validation rather than defensiveness. Parental reflective functioning (PRF) is thought to be a necessary precursor to such productive enactments. This study examined whether PRF during individual preparatory sessions with parents predicted parents' observed behaviors toward their young adult during subsequent conjoint sessions. Participants included 45 parents of Israeli LGBTQ+ young adults who participated in an open clinical trial of attachment-based family therapy for sexual and gender minorities. PRF was observationally coded using a modification of the Reflective Functioning Scale. Parents' behaviors were coded using the Parent-Child Interaction Coding System. Consistent with our preregistered hypothesis, higher levels of PRF in individual sessions with parents predicted a greater frequency of constructive parent behaviors toward their young adult, including validating the young adult's experience and soliciting their emotional reactions, during subsequent conjoint sessions. Conversely, higher PRF predicted significantly lower frequencies of parents' patronizing and judgmental behaviors. Contrary to our hypothesis, parents' defensiveness was not associated with PRF. Notably, PRF in the final preparatory session with parents remained a significant predictor of their behaviors in subsequent conjoint sessions, even when controlling for initial parental reflective functioning, suggesting that fostering mentalization immediately prior to conjoint sessions is a crucial therapeutic task. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Strategies for family caregivers experiencing anticipatory grief: a literature review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anticipatory grief is a common emotional response among family caregivers of individuals with a life-limiting illness. Unaddressed, it can lead to psychological distress and an impact on health and quality of life. AIMS: This literature review explores management strategies recommended for family caregivers who are experiencing anticipatory grief. METHODS: A systematic search of the literature was undertaken using CINAHL, Cochrane, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science. RESULTS: Three overarching themes emerged from the analysis: individual formal psychological therapy; social, community and health care support; and family therapy. CONCLUSIONS: A range of management approaches for anticipatory grief were identified, encompassing more structured therapeutic interventions, including psychological interviews, counselling, cognitive behavioural therapy and narrative therapy. Themes relating to social support were also identified, including opportunities to talk with others and having time away from the caregiver role.

papers.title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of an integrative psychotherapy incorporating an attachment-based approach for adolescents with cannabis use disorder (TIMCA).
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cannabis is the most used illicit substance among adolescents. Regular cannabis use is linked to cognitive and psychosocial difficulties. As no pharmacological treatment has proven effective, psychological interventions, including motivational interviewing (MI), cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), and family-based approaches, remain central. However, adolescent-specific evidence remains limited. TIMCA was developed as a ten-session integrative psychotherapy combining MI, CBT, and integrated attachment therapy. While family therapy may not be indicated for all adolescents, parental involvement remains important for the adolescent-parent relationship. TIMCA therefore combines individual and parent-adolescent sessions to address cannabis use alongside attachment-related and emotion-regulation processes. OBJECTIVES: This pilot randomized controlled trial evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of TIMCA and explored changes over time in cannabis use and relational, emotional, anxiety/depressive, and treatment-adherence outcomes compared with treatment as usual (TAU). METHODS: Thirty-nine adolescents with cannabis use disorder were randomly assigned to TIMCA (n = 19) or TAU (n = 20) in two outpatient addiction services in the Paris metropolitan area. Cannabis use, attachment security, emotion regulation, anxiety, and depressive symptoms were assessed at baseline, mid-treatment, post-treatment, and 1-month follow-up using self-report measures and urine toxicology. RESULTS: TIMCA was feasible and acceptable, with high treatment adherence. Exploratory analyses showed significant within-group changes, including reductions in cannabis use, emotion dysregulation, and depressive symptoms, along with improved attachment security. In TAU, within-group changes did not reach statistical significance, and no significant between-group differences were detected. CONCLUSION: TIMCA appears feasible and acceptable, supporting further evaluation

papers.title: Who determines the outcome? A three-level meta-analysis on systemic therapy in children and adolescents.
papers.journal: Psychotherapy research : journal of the Society for Psychotherapy Research
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Systemic therapy (ST) is a well-established treatment approach to reduce symptoms, yet its effects across outcome domains, informants, and assessment methods remain underexplored. METHOD: We conducted a systematic literature review in multiple databases (PsycINFO, Pubmed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL), including RCT-studies comparing ST with a psychosocial control treatment for diagnosed children or adolescents. We conducted a three-level meta-analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using an adaptation for psychotherapy. RESULTS: Overall, we included 44 studies, 370 effect sizes, and 4617 families. The overall effect size was small but significant (g = .16, CI [.09, .23], p < .0001). Contrary to expectations, informants and assessment methods were no significant moderators. Effects were comparable across outcome domains including family functioning (g = .12), caregivers' psychopathology (g = .12) and patient symptoms (g = .19). Outcomes were mostly based on self-report symptom questionnaires, limiting interpretability. CONCLUSION: Findings support that ST improves family functioning and caregivers' psychopathology, underscoring the need for more diverse outcomes.

papers.title: Childhood maltreatment and perceived partner responsiveness: A dyadic analysis of posttraumatic symptoms as a mediator.
papers.journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Childhood maltreatment (CM) is a critical risk factor for a wide range of long-term adverse outcomes, including marital distress; however, research on its dyadic effects on the marital system and the mechanisms underlying these effects remains limited. This study examined the dyadic associations between CM and perceived partner responsiveness (PPR), and the mediating role of posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSS). METHOD: A convenience sample of 277 mixed-sex, married couples completed self-report questionnaires. Analyses were conducted using the actor-partner interdependence model, which accounts for the dyadic effects between partners. RESULTS: We found significant associations between CM and lower PPR, mediated by PTSS in both men and women. In women, PTSS fully mediated the link between CM and PPR, while in men, PTSS only partially mediated this relationship. Furthermore, a unique pathway was found where women's CM experiences were indirectly associated with lower PPR in their male partners through women's PTSS, indicating cross-generation and cross-partner associations of CM. CONCLUSION: The study highlights PTSS as a pathway through which CM is associated with PPR, potentially straining emotional connection within intimate relationships. These findings suggest that trauma-informed couples therapy could be beneficial when a partner is exposed to CM. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Self-Resemblance and Activity-Aware Responsiveness in XR Companions: Effects on Relational Openness and Reflection.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics
papers.abstract: As virtual companions increasingly populate extended reality (XR) environments, they are evolving from simple interactive interfaces into socially co-present entities that accompany users during everyday activities. This shift raises broader questions about how users' immediate relational perceptions toward digital agents can emerge in physically situated XR interaction. Prior research in psychology suggests that people may become more willing to disclose personal thoughts and emotions when relational closeness is perceived and when conversational partners demonstrate awareness of their behaviors or experiences. These findings imply that both relational identification and behavioral responsiveness may encourage users to move from simple expression toward more personally open interaction. In XR environments, such relational cues may be conveyed through how companions embody identity-related signals and how they perceive and respond to users' ongoing actions. To address this gap, we introduce a modular XR companion framework that independently manipulates two design dimensions: self-resemblance and activity-aware responsiveness. We evaluate these dimensions within a physical-virtual expressive interaction context using LEGO flower arrangement, where users' affective states are naturally externalized through open-ended physical construction. Our findings show that self-resemblance was associated with higher self-reported disclosure, social intimacy, and social connectedness, while activity-aware responsiveness primarily supported self-reflection and longer interaction. This work reframes XR companion design from enhancing presence to supporting immediate relational openness and provides design insights for identity-reflective and activity-contingent interaction in physical-virtual environments.

papers.title: Breastfeeding and Genitourinary Symptoms: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Understanding genitourinary effects of breastfeeding allows for proactive treatments and quality-of-life improvements. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to estimate the effect of breastfeeding on genitourinary symptoms. STUDY DESIGN: This prospective cohort study of breastfeeding (BF) versus non-breastfeeding (NB) primiparous women characterized genitourinary symptoms after singleton delivery at ≥34 weeks of gestation. Validated measures included the Urinary Distress Inventory-6 (UDI-6), Incontinence Impact Questionnaire-7 (IIQ-7), Most Bothersome Symptom questionnaire (MBS), and Pelvic Organ Prolapse Incontinence Sexual Questionnaire, IUGA-Revised (PISQ-IR). Questionnaires were completed at baseline, 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months postpartum. The primary outcome was the UDI-6 score at 3 months. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were evaluated for group differences. RESULTS: UDI-6 scores at 3 months were not different between groups (5.6±11.8 BF, 7±12 NB, P=0.43). Differences in IIQ-7 scores were not statistically significant (4.9±7.4 BF, 13.5±25.2 NB, P=0.07). Multivariable analysis for those not sexually active revealed better partner-related scores in the BF group (β, -0.85; 95% CI, -1.58, -0.12, P=0.024). Among those sexually active, the BF group had worse condition impact scores (β, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.11, 0.47, P=0.002). The three-month MBS revealed nearly a threefold likelihood of experiencing vaginal dryness in BF (adjusted odds ratio, 2.82; 95% CI, 1.19, 6.66, P=0.018). At 6 months, vaginal dryness was no longer different, but breastfeeding continued to affect sexual function. CONCLUSIONS: At 3-months postpartum, there were no differences in lower urinary tract symptom severity between BF versus NB women. papers.title: A multimodal approach to sexual function after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Sexual dysfunction is a frequent long-term complication following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). This multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial evaluated the feasibility and efficacy of a multimodal intervention targeting sexual function and early detection of genital chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) in adult recipients of HSCT. Participants were randomized 1:1 to the intervention or usual care. The intervention included repeated questionnaires, genital assessments, and nurse-led consultations. Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index or the International Index of Erectile Function, with secondary outcomes including sexual health, sexual distress, and feasibility measures. Overall sexual function did not differ significantly between groups for women (difference (diff) 3.3, P = 0.391) or men (diff 0.9, P = 0.761). Significant improvements favoring the intervention group were observed in women's sexual pain (diff -2.1, P = 0.019) and, for both sexes, in sexual pain (diff -13.6, P = 0.030), communication with professionals (diff -15.5, P = 0.017), and partnership quality (diff -22.8, P = 0.040). The incidence of genital cGVHD was 25.0% among male (n = 11) and 28.1% (n = 9) among females. We conclude that the multimodal intervention was feasible, led to improved sexual health, and facilitated earlier recognition of genital cGVHD, supporting the integration of interdisciplinary sexual health assessments into routine post-HSCT care.

papers.title: Gender power dynamics and contraceptive decision-making among sexually active girls and young women in Nigeria.
papers.abstract: This qualitative study explored how gender power dynamics shape the decisions of girls and young women in Sagamu Local Government Area (Ogun State) and Benin City (Edo State), Nigeria, regarding romantic relationships, sexual activity, contraceptive use and pregnancy prevention. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 14 participants (7 pregnant young mothers and 7 sexually active non-mothers), recruited through criterion-based and snowball sampling. Thematic analysis revealed that financial dependence, emotional attachment and the need for companionship were key motivations for relationships. Although awareness of modern contraception was common, its use was limited by misconceptions, fear of side effects, male partner resistance and constrained negotiation ability. Gender power imbalances, exacerbated by age and economic disparities, fundamentally undermined reproductive autonomy. Nonetheless, glimpses of sexual and reproductive agency were evident in the active assertion of sexual desire and in the varied strategies participants employed to negotiate contraceptive use. Findings indicate that addressing adolescent pregnancy in Nigeria requires moving beyond contraceptive knowledge dissemination. Interventions must be gender-sensitive, empower girls and young women to negotiate sexual and reproductive decisions, and address underlying structural inequalities to strengthen relational autonomy.

papers.title: The Sexual Experiences of People Living with Sickle Cell Disease.
papers.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) affects over 8 million people globally and 1 in 365 Black infants in the United States are born with SCD. Because of recent medical advances, people are living significantly longer with SCD, with opportunities to experience romantic and sexual relationships. However, people with SCD experience medical challenges, such as pain crises, which can occur during partnered sexual activities. This study sought to understand how SCD impacts a person's sexual life. Using thematic analysis, 18 people, between 18 and 59 years old, gave an account of their experiences with solo masturbation and partnered sexual activities. Five themes were constructed: (1) Experiencing a Sex- or Orgasm-Induced Pain Crisis From Solo Masturbation and Partnered Sexual Activities; (2) Sexual Satisfaction and Orgasmic Pleasure; (3) Sickle Cell-Related Genital Pain With and Without Sexual Activity; (4) Intimate Connection With Sexual Partner; and (5) Communication About the Intersection of Sexuality and SCD. Overall, the participants described having satisfying experiences with solo masturbation and partnered sexual activities. However, a sex- or orgasm-induced pain crisis has impacted their sexual lives, including hospitalizations from said event. Additionally, participants experienced sickle cell-related genital pain with and without sexual activity.

papers.title: Cultural and social influences on women's experiences of sex and intimacy after cancer: 'I just think romance looks different'.
papers.abstract: Little is known about the influence of culture or membership of a minoritised group, on the sexual health of women with cancer. The goal of this study was to explore sexual health and relationship experiences of diverse women cancer survivors. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eleven partnered women surviving cancer who self-identified as members of a minoritised group, including sexual minorities, immigrants, and women of colour, with ages ranging from 28 to 64 years. Just over half the participants had had breast cancer (n = 7; 63%). Data were subjected to interpretive thematic analysis. Themes and subthemes are developed under four main headings: 1) sexual influencers prior to cancer experience; 2) impacts of diagnosis and treatment on relationships, sex and sexuality; 3) bodily impacts after cancer treatment; and 4) survivors and partners navigating discussions of sex. Perceptions and behaviours related to sexual health and intimacy were influenced by family, religion, culture, and social structures among women surviving cancer. Sexual health is an integral part of cancer survivorship care and because of this, services should be tailored to meet the sexual health needs of diverse women.

papers.title: The Storied Narratives of Partners of Those Who Have Undergone a Prostatectomy.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer is perceived as a "couple's disease"; the diagnosis and treatment impact the patient-partner relationship. OBJECTIVE: To explore the storied narratives of a partner and their relationship with their loved one who has undergone a radical prostatectomy (RP) to treat prostate cancer. METHODS: This qualitative interpretive study used narrative analysis to understand how participants construct stories and narratives from their personal experiences. This approach provides insight into the partners' experiences, relationship changes post-RP, and barriers. RESULTS: Two overarching themes emerged: (1) partners' experience with the cancer diagnosis and (2) partners' experience with RP treatment. Seven main themes emerged as areas of significance related to the patient-partner relationship: (1) changing the relationship, (2) intimacy (including sexual and emotional intimacy), (3) desire for support, (4) managing disruption, (5) loss of control, (6) elevating partner's needs, and (7) protecting affected partner. CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that the post-RP relationship between the participant and their loved one improved or stayed the same; however, the sexual intimacy was negatively impacted, whereas the emotional intimacy was deepened. This study's findings highlight the need for ongoing education, resources, and support for the partner. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Support resources must be cultivated and offered to partners, and a "projected timeline" must be created to assist partners in managing the disruption and the feeling of loss of control. Incorporating relationship and caregiver counseling, sex education, and therapy can significantly impact the post-RP relationship.

papers.title: Exploring Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) Symptomatology in Relation to Women's Orgasmic Consistency.
papers.abstract: This well-powered, pre-registered online study examined differences in orgasmic consistency among women both with and without ADHD symptomatology while controlling for sexual assertiveness and sexual attitudes, constructs yet to be explored in this context. A convenience sample of 815 (Mage = 28.93, SDage = 9.23) cisgender females, at least 18 years of age and sexually active with at least one partner over the last 6 months, completed this study online through the survey platform Qualtrics. No preexisting ADHD diagnosis was required. Study hypotheses were confirmed, revealing that ADHD symptomatology predicted orgasmic consistency, and most notably, that greater inattentive ADHD symptomatology was associated with lower consistency of orgasm. Exploration of medication use for ADHD symptom management revealed only a significant effect of medication use on orgasmic consistency in women who did not currently meet the criteria for ADHD symptomatology. Finally, when comparing women of sexual minority orientations to the sexual majority, results indicated only a significant difference in orgasmic consistency rates among women who did not meet the ADHD symptomatology criteria. Given that women who struggle with difficulties in consistently achieving orgasm are more likely to experience negative relationship satisfaction, self-esteem, and sexual satisfaction outcomes - as well as increased rates of emotional distress - our results have significant implications for the sexual health and well-being of women with ADHD symptomatology. This is particularly true for those with the inattentive ADHD symptomatology subtype.

papers.title: Coercive Control Through Religious Authority: Intimate Partner Violence in the Israeli Ultra-Orthodox Community.
papers.abstract: While intimate partner violence (IPV) has increasingly been examined in religious collectivist contexts, limited theoretical attention has been given to culturally embedded patterns of coercive control within such settings. This study examines IPV against ultra-Orthodox (UO) Jewish women in Israel, asking: What culturally embedded mechanisms characterize this violence, and how do UO social workers interpret them? Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 16 UO social workers (nine women and seven men) with professional training and insider cultural knowledge, thematic analysis identified recurring non-physical patterns of domination. IPV appeared to operate through four culturally structured mechanisms: silent treatment, spiritual coercion, sexism, and financial control, all within a pervasive climate of emotional violence. These findings extend coercive control scholarship by distinguishing between macro-level communal rewards and micro-level interpersonal recognition within patriarchal bargains, demonstrating how their divergence may produce layered entrapment in religious collectivist settings. More broadly, the study situates IPV within intersecting structures of gendered and minority marginalization and highlights how symbolic religious authority may function as a culturally legitimate way of sustaining domination even in the absence of physical violence or material dependency.

papers.title: Intimate Partner Violence Around the Time of Pregnancy and Infant Safe Sleep Practices.
papers.abstract: Does intimate partner violence (IPV) before or during pregnancy increase the likelihood of unsafe infant sleep practices (surface sharing and non-supine positioning) among women with a recent live birth? The sample included 213,556 women with a recent live birth participating in the 2016 to 2022 Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) from 41 U.S. jurisdictions. We analyzed PRAMS data to estimate the prevalence of physical IPV 12 months before or during pregnancy and infant sleep practices (i.e., surface sharing and supine positioning) by demographic characteristics. We calculated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) to examine associations between physical IPV and infant sleep practices. Overall, 3.2% (95% confidence interval [CI] [3.1, 3.3]) of women reported physical IPV in the 12 months before or during pregnancy. Experiences of physical IPV in the 12 months before or during pregnancy were significantly associated with an increased likelihood of reporting surface sharing in the 2 weeks before survey administration and those who had experienced physical IPV had 20% higher odds of putting their infant in a non-supine sleep position compared to those who had not experienced IPV (aOR = 1.2, 95% CI [1.1, 1.4]). Physical IPV before or during pregnancy may be an important risk factor for unsafe infant sleep practices. Attention to IPV as a potential barrier to safe infant sleep practices may be an important consideration for perinatal care and support.

papers.title: Psychiatric Comorbidity, Personality Disorders and Intimate Partner Violence Among Men With Alcohol Use Disorder: Independent Correlates and Exploratory Risk Profiles From North India.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is common among men with alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the relative contributions of psychiatric comorbidity, personality disorders and dependence severity remain uncertain. We explored the prevalence and correlates of IPV perpetration among treatment-seeking men with AUD. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 100 consecutive men with AUD attending a tertiary psychiatry service in North India were assessed using the Severity of Alcohol Dependence Questionnaire (SADQ), Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview, Millon Clinical Multiaxial Inventory-III and the World Health Organization Domestic Violence Questionnaire. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent correlates of IPV; exploratory analyses examined IPV prevalence across combinations of dependence severity, psychiatric comorbidity and personality disorders. RESULTS: Forty-one percent reported IPV perpetration in the preceding 12 months. Psychiatric comorbidity (adjusted odds ratio 6.66, 95% confidence interval 2.10, 21.11), personality disorder (adjusted odds ratio 6.26, 95% confidence interval 1.79, 21.92) and alcohol-use duration > 10 years (adjusted odds ratio 5.96, 95% confidence interval 1.55, 22.84) were independently associated with IPV; SADQ severity was not (adjusted odds ratio 2.34, p = 0.062). IPV prevalence was highest among participants with both psychiatric comorbidity and personality disorder (21 of 22; 95.5%). Among those with psychiatric comorbidity, IPV prevalence was consistently high (75%-77%) across SADQ severity categories. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: Psychiatric comorbidity and personality disorders were more strongly associated with IPV perpetration than dependence severity. Routine psychiatric assessment may help identify patients at elevated IPV risk. Prospective studies are needed to establish temporal relationships and whether treating comorbid conditions reduces

papers.title: Transcriptomic Network Analysis Reveals Trauma Type- and Ancestry-Related Heterogeneity in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a debilitating psychiatric disorder that frequently co-occurs with major depressive disorder (MDD), a comorbidity that is partly attributable to shared genetic heritability and common environmental risk factors. Despite extensive efforts to identify peripheral transcriptomic biomarkers, findings have been inconsistent, potentially reflecting the substantial biological heterogeneity underlying these disorders. The primary goal of this study was to identify molecular signatures that reflect the clinical and biological heterogeneity of PTSD and MDD. METHODS: The authors present a network analysis of blood-based transcriptomics from 466 pregnant women in South Africa, including 215 individuals with PTSD and/or MDD (mean age, 26.34 years [SD=5.77]) and 251 trauma-exposed control participants (mean age, 27.14 years [SD=5.82]). Gene expression modules associated with trauma-related phenotypes were identified, including childhood adversity, intimate partner violence, and recent life stress, as well as ancestry and depressive symptoms, highlighting multiple sources of molecular variation. To evaluate the predictive relevance of these transcriptomic features, random forest models were applied using a nested cross-validation framework with permutation testing. RESULTS: Models achieved moderate and statistically significant performance in predicting trauma-related phenotypes (mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC], ~0.61-0.69 across models [SD=0.07-0.10]), whereas prediction of PTSD or MDD diagnosis showed near-chance performance (mean AUROC=0.52, SD=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures are more strongly associated with trauma exposure profiles and population background than with diagnostic status. Collectively, the results support exposure-informed stratification as a complementary framework to traditional diagnostic categories for capturing bio

papers.title: The lived experience of intimate partner violence among first-generation latino immigrants in Southern New Mexico.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a significant public health concern that disproportionately affects immigrant populations. First-generation Latino immigrants in the United States experience IPV within complex cultural, relational, and structural contexts that remain underexplored. This study aimed to explore and describe how first-generation Latino immigrants in Southern New Mexico experience and make meaning of IPV and to examine the cultural and relational influences shaping these experiences. A qualitative phenomenological design was used, and reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines. Twenty-four first-generation Latino immigrants were interviewed; two who described observing rather than personally experiencing IPV were excluded, yielding an analytic sample of 22 who participated in in-depth, semi-structured interviews conducted in English or Spanish using a trauma-informed and culturally responsive approach. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and translated where necessary. Data was analyzed using thematic analysis informed by phenomenological principles, supported by Intellectus® Qualitative software and manual coding to ensure rigor and depth. Data saturation was reached during data collection. Six major themes emerged: cultural factors, abuse, culture of silence, control, universal factors, and systemic barriers to legal and support resources. Participants described IPV as shaped by cultural norms, normalization of violence, fear, dependency, and limited access to resources. A pervasive culture of silence, reinforced by stigma, immigration-related fears, and social isolation, constrained help-seeking behaviors. Structural barriers further limited access to legal protections and support systems, exacerbating vulnerability. Findings highlight the need for culturally responsive, multilevel interventions that address the social, cultural, and structural determinants of IPV among

papers.title: Perspectives on traumatic brain injury screening among intersecting underserved populations: an exploratory study.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to explore barriers and facilitators in traumatic brain injury (TBI) screening for underserved individuals and knowledge translation efforts to address challenges. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Guided by qualitative description, we conducted four virtual focus groups: 10 people (7 female, 3 male) with lived experience of precarious housing, criminal legal involvement, and/or violence and 11 service providers (9 female, 2 male) supporting these populations with TBI. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. FINDINGS: Barriers to TBI screening included (1) inconsistent implementation and competing priorities within organizations; (2) stigmatization and systemic challenges in service provision; and (3) a lack of a universal screening system and follow-up pathways. While potential facilitators to screening involved language, knowledge and resources, as identified in the following themes: (1) language matters: shaping conversations in TBI screening; (2) screening for all: knowledge and access; and (3) easy and engaging tools for screening. CONCLUSIONS: Barriers to TBI screening persist. Systemic changes and targeted educational initiatives are needed to improve knowledge and awareness of TBI with sensitivity to potential circumstances of specific populations. Affirming conversational language in screening, along with providing tailored resources and access to follow-up support services that address social determinants of health, are essential.

papers.title: Exploring the Role of Alcohol in the Association Between Problematic Pornography Use and Sexual Intimate Partner Violence Perpetration Among College Students.
papers.abstract: Emerging data suggest problematic pornography use is associated with sexual violence perpetration, though limited research has examined this association within intimate partners. One known correlate of college students' sexual intimate partner violence (IPV) perpetration that may influence the degree to which problematic pornography use relates to sexual IPV is alcohol use and problems. This study tested the hypothesis that problematic pornography use would positively relate to sexual IPV perpetration among undergraduates with high, but not low, levels of alcohol use and problems. College students (N = 236; 67.4% women, 77.5% white) completed an online survey assessing problematic pornography use, alcohol use and problems, and sexual IPV perpetration. We estimated the moderating effect of alcohol use and problems on the association between problematic pornography use and sexual IPV perpetration while statistically controlling for sex assigned at birth. The interaction between problematic pornography use and alcohol use and problems was significantly related to sexual IPV perpetration (B = 0.03, SE = 0.01, p = .01) such that problematic pornography use was positively associated with sexual IPV perpetration among participants with higher, but not lower, levels of alcohol use and problems. Problematic pornography use combined with greater alcohol use and problems in college students was associated with more frequent sexual IPV perpetration. Increased education on responsible alcohol and pornography use may mitigate sexual IPV perpetration risk among college students.

papers.title: "A Good Idea in an Ideal World": Survivors' Views on Restorative Justice for Intimate Partner Violence.
papers.abstract: In response to longstanding critiques of the legal system's ability to meet survivors' justice-related needs, restorative justice (RJ) has been proposed as a complementary approach that emphasizes healing, accountability, and survivor participation. However, the use of RJ in cases of intimate partner violence (IPV) remains highly contested, with concerns surrounding safety, power imbalances, coercion, and the potential for re-traumatization. Despite these debates, there is limited empirical research examining how survivors themselves perceive the suitability of RJ in the context of IPV. Drawing on in-depth interviews with 57 women and nonbinary survivors of IPV in Ontario, Canada, this study explores their willingness to engage in RJ processes and perceived benefits and risks. Using a community-engaged research approach, findings reveal substantial variation in survivors' views. Participants identified potential benefits of RJ, including having a voice, achieving closure, holding perpetrators accountable, involving the community, and preventing future harm. At the same time, many expressed significant concerns related to personal safety, the sincerity of perpetrator accountability, and the adequacy of community capacity to support restorative processes. Overall, survivors tended to view RJ as an idealized model of justice, with practical benefits contingent upon stringent safeguards. The paper concludes by situating findings within ongoing debates about RJ and IPV, and by offering recommendations for practice and future research grounded in survivors' lived experiences.

papers.title: Well-Being Among Latine Survivors of Intimate Partner Violence: A Systematic Review of Protective Factors and Resilience Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Despite evidence that Latine intimate partner violence (IPV) survivors demonstrate well-being across multiple life domains, limited research has examined the processes through which protective factors contribute to resilience in this population. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review guided by the Resilience Portfolio Model, which categorizes strengths as regulatory, interpersonal-ecological, and meaning-making and identifies additive, buffering, and inoculating mechanisms through which they operate. We searched PsycINFO, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, Violence and Abuse Abstracts, PubMed, and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses, supplemented by gray literature and manual reference checks. Forty-seven studies met inclusion criteria. Additive mechanisms were most frequently identified across all strength categories, with spiritual practices, social support, culturally tailored programs, and motherhood emerging as central to well-being. Buffering mechanisms were supported by limited evidence, including cognitive reappraisal and supportive familism. Inoculation mechanisms were identified in strategies that protected against re-victimization, such as boundary-setting and legal protections. Findings underscore that resilience is not solely an individual process but is deeply embedded in cultural, relational, and structural contexts. Cultural values operated as both resources and constraints, highlighting their conditional role. The reviewed literature predominantly reflects the experiences of adult immigrant Latina survivors, limiting generalizability to other subgroups. Future research should prioritize longitudinal designs and explicit testing of resilience mechanisms. Policies and interventions should adopt culturally responsive, multi-level approaches that strengthen individual, relational, and structural resources for Latine IPV survivors.

papers.title: Special Issue Introduction Festschrift in Honor of Jon Conte's Retirement as Editor of the Journal of Interpersonal Violence: The Future of Interpersonal Violence Research.
papers.abstract: Founding Editor Jon Conte asked colleagues in the field to write a short piece on their thoughts about next steps to move research forward, research questions that should be addressed over the next 5 years, or next steps toward prevention. The articles in this Festschrift will hopefully provide ideas for our colleagues in the near future to guide our responses and move the field forward toward eradication of interpersonal violence.

papers.title: Increasing Language Access for Intimate Partner Violence Support Services: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a significant public health concern. Survivors face numerous barriers to accessing services, particularly when services in many places are only provided in English. This scoping review aimed to identify research and practice-based articles that explore interventions to increase language accessibility to support services for IPV. Articles were identified through a systematic search of databases and selected for inclusion if they involved language accessibility for IPV support services across settings (e.g., legal services, advocacy, hotlines, social services, healthcare, law enforcement). We identified 15 research and 14 practice-based articles for inclusion. Most interventions and practices for increasing language access were in settings related to health care, advocacy and social services, or community-based organizations. Research articles described various adaptations to interventions for increasing language access, which mostly included interpretation, translation, bilingual assistance, and culturally tailored programs. All research articles had language access adaptations for their intervention, but only 60% of the research articles included specific findings related to language access and culture. Practice-based articles discussed guidance around the development, assessment, and evaluation of a language access plan, language access engagement and implementation, and different elements and settings for language access. Findings highlight the intersection between language and culture, underscoring the need to address these interconnected aspects beyond simple translation and interpretation. IPV support services should hire multilingual and multicultural staff and address fear around immigration status. Increased funding is needed to ensure higher quality language access supports are implemented. Additional implications for research, practice, and policy are discussed.

papers.title: Contraceptive method choice by type of intimate partner violence: findings from the 2015 Colombian demographic and health survey.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major global health issue and limits women's reproductive autonomy. Despite high IPV and contraception prevalences in Colombia, the link between specific types of IPV and contraceptive methods remains understudied. This study aimed to examine associations between IPV and the type of contraceptive method used by Colombian women. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the 2015 Colombian Demographic and Health Surveys. The sample included 13,896 ever-partnered women aged 15-49 who were not pregnant, infecund, or used permanent methods. Contraceptive method was categorised as: no contraception, traditional/fertility awareness methods (FAM), intrauterine devices (IUDs)/implants, oral/injectables, and external condoms. Exposure variables included any IPV, physical, sexual and emotional violence, and controlling behaviour in the past 12 months. Adjusted multinomial logistic regressions were conducted, with a significance level of p < 0.05. RESULTS: Physical and emotional IPV were associated with higher relative risks of using traditional/FAMs and IUDs/implants, and lower probabilities of using oral/injectables or external condoms. Sexual IPV was associated with higher relative risk and controlling behaviour with lower relative risk of using all contraceptive methods. CONCLUSIONS: IPV-exposed women were more likely to use long-acting methods that can be used covertly, are less susceptible to partner interference, and require fewer healthcare visits, which may reflect increased contraceptive vigilance. Understanding the impact of IPV on contraceptive methods is necessary to improve women's reproductive autonomy. Integrating IPV screening into family planning services and further research into contraceptive decision-making in abusive relationships is recommended. papers.title: Psychopathological and neuropsychological sequelae in children victimised by intimate partner violence: a clinical case series.
papers.abstract: Background: Childhood exposure to intimate partner violence against women (IPVAW) is recognised as a form of maltreatment with lasting emotional, cognitive, and neurobiological consequences. Despite evidence of disruptions in executive functioning, attention, and memory, clinical case-based research remains scarce, particularly during middle childhood.Objective: This study examined psychopathological and neuropsychological sequelae of IPVAW - including witnessing violence and direct psychological, physical, and/or sexual abuse - through a clinical case series.Method: Four children aged 5-9 with documented IPVAW exposure underwent comprehensive clinical and neuropsychological assessment.Results: All children showed significant internalising symptoms, emotional dysregulation, and trauma-related distress. Cognitive profiles revealed selective impairments, especially in executive functioning, attention, and processing speed, while general intelligence was preserved. Greater exposure severity and polyvictimization were associated with more complex symptom patterns.Conclusions: IPVAW exposure is linked to pervasive emotional and cognitive difficulties. Findings underscore the need for early, multidimensional assessments and targeted interventions addressing both psychopathology and neuropsychological consequences. Children exposed to intimate partner violence show consistent emotional suffering, including anxiety, fear responses, and difficulties managing their emotions, even when they do not experience direct abuse.Neuropsychological assessment revealed selective cognitive difficulties, especially in attention, working memory, and executive functions, while overall intelligence remained within the expected range for their age.The severity and combination of different forms of violence were linked to more complex psychological and cognitive difficulties, highlighting the need for early and comprehensive evaluations to guide clinical and legal decisions.

papers.title: Research Priorities for Responding to Sexual Victimization of Children and of Adults: A Backlash Against Believing the Victim and the Research.
papers.abstract: Sexual abuse victimization of both children and adults is too common, yet significant gaps remain in the available research to support professionals who are conducting investigations, evaluating disclosures, assessing credibility, and involved in the decision-making that happens in legal, law enforcement, mental health, and institutional settings. This article examines the current available research and what should be prioritized in future research across three overlapping areas: childhood sexual abuse (CSA), particularly in families where intimate partner violence (IPV) is also present and family-court involvement occurs; sexual assault of adults in criminal and civil legal contexts; and adult survivors of CSA, including those abused within institutional settings. Several issues present themselves across these populations that warrant further study. These include: delayed disclosure and delayed recall; the effects of trauma on memory and how memory is being understood by investigators and others; betrayal trauma and institutional betrayal; victim blaming and disbelief; and the responses of deny, attack, and reverse victim and offender (DARVO) by alleged offenders and the effects on alleged victims and other parties involved in these cases. The current research is also limited by dated literature, inconsistent terminology being used in these cases, research models that may not adequately reflect the circumstances in which traumatic experiences are disclosed and recalled, and relatively little longitudinal research examining legal and institutional responses to the complex dynamics of these cases. This article identifies priorities for future research, advocating for more ecologically valid studies, greater consistency in definitions and methodology, longitudinal investigations, closer examination of professional and judicial decision-making, and further study of the overlap between CSA and IPV. papers.title: The moderating effects of social norms and attitudes on the relationship between intimate partner violence and depressive symptoms among women in two provinces of Nepal.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is often associated with increased depressive symptoms. However, considerable variability exists in this relationship, from null findings to large effect estimates, likely due, in part, to differences in attitudes (thoughts and beliefs), descriptive norms (perceptions of what behaviors occur in a community), and injunctive norms (perceptions of what behaviors are acceptable in a community). In this study, we test the effect of individual- and community-level attitudes and norms on the IPV-depressive symptoms relationship. METHODS: The sample included 976 married women in 30 communities in Nepal. We measured depressive symptoms with the Patient Health Questionnaire and IPV with items adapted from the Revised Conflict Tactics Scale. We used generalized linear models to test seven moderators: individual-level attitudes (gender-inequitability and acceptability of husband abuse), an individual-level descriptive norms scale, and community-level proxies of injunctive norms (aggregated attitudes) and descriptive norms (aggregated IPV prevalence and descriptive norms scale). RESULTS: Descriptive norms significantly moderated the IPV-depressive symptoms relationship at both the individual and community level. The differences in depressive symptoms between women who did and did not experience IPV were stronger where violence was perceived to be less widespread. Individual-level attitudes and community-level injunctive norms proxies were not found to be significant moderators. CONCLUSION: Where IPV is less prevalent (or perceived as such), experiencing IPV may increase depressive symptoms, as the experience deviates from the prevailing norm. Research should continue to refine norms measurement and explore individual and contextual factors that impact the likelihood of negative mental health outcomes to inform prevention and response interventions.

papers.title: Burden and trends of anxiety, depressive, and bipolar disorders in China from 1990 to 2023: Joinpoint, age-period-cohort effects, and forecasts.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anxiety disorders, depressive disorders, and bipolar disorder are major contributors to global disability and functional impairment. Updated evidence on temporal trends, demographic patterns, and projected burden is needed to characterise the population-level burden of these disorders in China. METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates, we assessed disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) counts and age-standardised DALY rates (ASDRs) for anxiety disorders, depressive disorders, and bipolar disorder in China from 1990 to 2023. We described age- and sex-specific DALY patterns in 2023, evaluated ASDR trends using Joinpoint regression, examined age-, period-, and cohort-related patterns using an age-period-cohort estimable-function framework, and decomposed changes in DALY counts into contributions from population growth, population ageing, and epidemiological change. Bayesian age-period-cohort modelling was used to project ASDRs for 2024-2038. We characterised attributable DALY burden for violence- and trauma-related risk factors across applicable disorder-exposure pairs. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, ASDRs increased overall for anxiety disorders and depressive disorders, whereas bipolar-disorder ASDRs remained comparatively stable. Anxiety-disorder burden showed a younger age distribution, whereas depressive-disorder burden was more concentrated in middle-to-older adulthood; bipolar-disorder burden was primarily concentrated in midlife. Females generally had higher age-standardised DALY rates than males across all three disorders, with sex disparities largest for anxiety and depressive disorders. Decomposition analyses indicated distinct contributions of population growth, population ageing, and epidemiological change across disorders. Projections suggested a continued increase in the anxiety-disorder ASDR, an initial increase followed by stabilisation or gradual decline in the depressive-disorder ASDR, and a relatively stable bipolar-disorde

papers.title: The science of child and adolescent mental health in Mozambique: A systematic review of prevalence estimates, measurement tools, and interventions.
papers.abstract: Mozambique is home to 18 million children and adolescents largely underrepresented in mental health research. We conducted a systematic review of evidence-based resources (prevalence estimates, assessment instruments, and interventions) on mental health-related outcomes addressing individuals aged 0-19 years in Mozambique. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Google Scholar, African Index Medicus, and local catalogues. Extraction followed COSMIN and Cochrane manuals (PROSPERO registration: CRD420251016208). The search yielded 81 unique publications, including 61 reports presenting prevalence estimates from 25 studies, 29 reports providing data on 42 assessment instruments, and 9 intervention reports describing 8 intervention trials. The clinical prevalence of mental disorders were estimated in two surveys, conducted in Nampula (ADHD: 13·4%; N = 748, 6-18 years) and Maputo (any mental diagnosis: 23%, anxiety disorders: 17·5%; major depression episode: 8·5%; disruptive behavior disorder: 6·6%; substance use disorders: 4·5%; ADHD: 3·3%; PTSD: 1·2%; N = 486, 12-19 years). Most research focused on psychosocial adversities, with nationally representative adolescent surveys reporting significant exposure to violence (physical/emotional violence annually: 24·86%; girls suffering intimate partner violence: 21·11%; lifetime sexual abuse: 16·55%). National suicide rates were highest among 15-19-year-olds (1·53 per 100,000). Only four instruments were cross-culturally adapted and showed reliable psychometrics (MINI-KID, GAD-7, PHQ-A, and SDQ), whilst unadapted tools performed poorly. There was a single randomized clinical trial which reported a cost-effective intervention for neurodevelopment among high-poverty preschoolers.
